title: Repentance
definition: Repentance is a Spirit-enabled turning from sin to God with sorrow for sin, confession, and a renewed desire to obey Him.
summary: Repentance turns from sin and returns to God through the mercy offered in Christ.
christFocus: Jesus calls sinners to repent and receive forgiveness, and His grace makes true turning possible.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Repentance is not mere regret, embarrassment, or fear of consequences. It is a real turning of the heart from sin to God. True repentance includes sorrow for sin, confession, hatred of evil, and movement toward obedience.

Repentance is not opposed to grace. It is a gift and response produced by God's work in the heart. The Gospel calls sinners to turn because forgiveness is found in Christ.

Believers continue to practice repentance throughout the Christian life. Repentance keeps the heart humble, honest, and dependent on mercy.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People often confuse repentance with shame or with trying harder after failure. This doctrine matters because it shows that God calls sinners not to despair but to return to Him through Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Confess sin honestly and turn toward God without delay. Do not excuse, hide, or rename what Scripture calls sin. Trust Christ's mercy and take concrete steps of obedience and accountability.
